conversations.answer: The error you're seeing is pretty explicit. It's being raised from the contentful library, specifically indicating that it expected the accessToken parameter when creating a client, but didn't receive it.Here's what you can do to resolve the issue:Environment Variables: Ensure that all environment variables used in your server.js are set properly. It seems process.env.REACT_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN is not available or undefined when the script is run. This is the root cause of the issue you're seeing..env File: If you're trying to use a .env file to load your environment variables (a common approach with Node.js applications), you'll need the dotenv package:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Then, at the very top of your server.js file, you'll need to configure dotenv:[CODE_BLOCK_1]Check .env File: Ensure you have a .env file in the root of your project and it contains the necessary keys:[CODE_BLOCK_2]... and so on.Logging: Add some logging right before creating the Contentful client to see if the values are being picked up:[CODE_BLOCK_3]Hardcoded Fallback: While it's not recommended for production, you can temporarily hardcode the ACCESS_TOKEN (and other values) to see if it works. This way, you'll be sure the issue lies with how the environment variables are loaded.[CODE_BLOCK_4]Lastly, always be cautious about hardcoding or logging sensitive tokens, especially in production or public-facing scenarios. If you ever commit them accidentally, be sure to invalidate the old tokens and generate new ones to prevent potential misuse.
